In the opinion of the Company&#8217;s management, the condensed consolidated financial statements reflect all adjustments, which are normal and recurring in nature, necessary for fair financial statement presentation. Actual results could differ materially from those estimates. Certain prior period amounts in the condensed consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes have been reclassified to conform to the current period&#8217;s presentation. The Company did not restate total net sales in the prior periods presented, as adoption of the new revenue standard did not have a material impact on previously reported amounts.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Additionally, beginning in the first quarter of 2019, the Company classified the amortization of the deferred value of Maps, Siri</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt">&#174;</sup></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> and free iCloud</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt">&#174;</sup></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> services, which are bundled in the sales price of iPhone</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt">&#174;</sup></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, Mac</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt">&#174;</sup></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, iPad</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt">&#174;</sup></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> and certain other products, in services net sales. The Company records restricted marketable securities as current or non-current marketable securities in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets based on the classification of the underlying securities.</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></span></div><div><a id="sFFBB791665D65C76811A9DCB768101DA"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 2 &#8211; <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerTextBlock" id="TextSelection-56E78E41ABE2572892B7E0E0DC6845BB-0-wk-Fact-0B0FF259ED3B5B7A83DB2AE393343468" continuedAt="TextSelection-56E78E41ABE2572892B7E0E0DC6845BB-1" escape="true">Revenue Recognition</ix:nonNumeric></span></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-56E78E41ABE2572892B7E0E0DC6845BB-1" continuedAt="TextSelection-56E78E41ABE2572892B7E0E0DC6845BB-2"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD" name="us-gaap:RevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock" id="TextSelection-326B9DD94A8C5048A7C675DBC3ECD37E-0-wk-Fact-E60E0CA545AB59A39C0C2730F1A66B41" continuedAt="TextSelection-326B9DD94A8C5048A7C675DBC3ECD37E-1" escape="true">Net sales consist of revenue from the sale of iPhone, Mac, iPad, services and other products. The Company recognizes revenue at the amount to which it expects to be entitled when control of the products or services is transferred to its customers. Control is generally transferred when the Company has a present right to payment and title and the significant risks and rewards of ownership of products or services are transferred to its customers. For most of the Company&#8217;s products net sales, control transfers when products are shipped. For the Company&#8217;s services net sales, control transfers over time as services are delivered. Payment for products and services net sales is collected within a short period of time following transfer of control or commencement of delivery of services, as applicable.</ix:nonNumeric></span></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-326B9DD94A8C5048A7C675DBC3ECD37E-1" continuedAt="TextSelection-326B9DD94A8C5048A7C675DBC3ECD37E-2"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company records reductions to products net sales related to future product returns, price protection and other customer incentive programs based on the Company&#8217;s expectations and historical experience.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">For arrangements with multiple performance obligations, which represent promises within an arrangement that are capable of being distinct, the Company allocates revenue to all distinct performance obligations based on their relative stand-alone selling prices (&#8220;SSP&#8221;). When available, the Company uses observable prices to determine the SSP. When observable prices are not available, SSPs are established that reflect the Company&#8217;s best estimates of what the selling prices of the performance obligations would be if they were sold regularly on a stand-alone basis. The Company&#8217;s process for estimating SSPs without observable prices considers multiple factors that may vary depending upon the unique facts and circumstances related to each performance obligation including, where applicable, prices charged by the Company for similar offerings, market trends in the pricing for similar offerings, product-specific business objectives and the estimated cost to provide the performance obligation.</span></div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">Apple Inc. | Q2 2019 Form 10-Q | </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">7</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><br/></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-56E78E41ABE2572892B7E0E0DC6845BB-2" continuedAt="TextSelection-56E78E41ABE2572892B7E0E0DC6845BB-3"><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-326B9DD94A8C5048A7C675DBC3ECD37E-2" continuedAt="TextSelection-326B9DD94A8C5048A7C675DBC3ECD37E-3"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company has identified up to </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><span><ix:nonFraction id="d41132817e439-wk-Fact-9FDE1A8892FA5C188B2271BCCCA3229B" name="aapl:PerformanceObligationsinArrangements" contextRef="FI2019Q2" unitRef="obligation" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">three</ix:nonFraction></span></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> performance obligations regularly included in arrangements involving the sale of iPhone, Mac, iPad and certain other products. The first performance obligation, which represents the substantial portion of the allocated sales price, is the hardware and bundled software delivered at the time of sale. The second performance obligation is the right to receive certain product-related bundled services, which include iCloud, Siri and Maps. The third performance obligation is the right to receive, on a when-and-if-available basis, future unspecified software upgrades relating to the software bundled with each device. The Company allocates revenue and any related discounts to these performance obligations based on their relative SSPs. Because the Company lacks observable prices for the undelivered performance obligations, the allocation of revenue is based on the Company&#8217;s estimated SSPs. Revenue allocated to the delivered hardware and bundled software is recognized when control has transferred to the customer, which generally occurs when the product is shipped. Revenue allocated to the product-related bundled services and unspecified software upgrade rights is deferred and recognized on a straight-line basis over the estimated period they are expected to be provided. Cost of sales related to delivered hardware and bundled software, including estimated warranty costs, are recognized at the time of sale. Costs incurred to provide product-related bundled services and unspecified software upgrade rights are recognized as cost of sales as incurred.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">For certain long-term service arrangements, the Company has performance obligations for services it has not yet delivered. For these arrangements, the Company does not have a right to bill for the undelivered services. The Company has determined that any unbilled consideration relates entirely to the value of the undelivered services. Accordingly, the Company has not recognized revenue, and has elected not to disclose amounts, related to these undelivered services.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">For the sale of third-party products where the Company obtains control of the product before transferring it to the customer, the Company recognizes revenue based on the gross amount billed to customers. The Company considers multiple factors when determining whether it obtains control of third-party products including, but not limited to, evaluating if it has the ability to establish the price of the product, retains inventory risk for tangible products or has the responsibility for ensuring acceptability of the product. For third-party applications sold through the App Store</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt">&#174;</sup></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, Mac App Store and TV App Store and certain digital content sold through the iTunes Store</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt">&#174;</sup></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, the Company does not obtain control of the product before transferring it to the customer. Therefore, the Company accounts for such sales on a net basis by recognizing in services net sales only the commission it retains.</span></div></ix:continuation><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><ix:continuation continuedAt="TextSelection-16E5C86F1D2C5813BC99BB86CBBE153D-1">Derivative Financial Instruments</ix:continuation></span></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-16E5C86F1D2C5813BC99BB86CBBE153D-1" continuedAt="TextSelection-16E5C86F1D2C5813BC99BB86CBBE153D-2"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company may use derivatives to partially offset its business exposure to foreign currency and interest rate risk on expected future cash flows, net investments in certain foreign subsidiaries, and certain existing assets and liabilities. However, the Company may choose not to hedge certain exposures for a variety of reasons including, but not limited to, accounting considerations or the prohibitive economic cost of hedging particular exposures. There can be no assurance the hedges will offset more than a portion of the financial impact resulting from movements in foreign currency exchange or interest rates.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">To protect gross margins from fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, certain of the Company&#8217;s subsidiaries whose functional currency is the U.S. dollar may hedge a portion of forecasted foreign currency revenue, and subsidiaries whose functional currency is not the U.S. dollar may hedge a portion of forecasted inventory purchases not denominated in the subsidiaries&#8217; functional currencies. The Company may enter into forward contracts, option contracts or other instruments to manage this risk and may designate these instruments as cash flow hedges. The Company generally hedges portions of its forecasted foreign currency exposure associated with revenue and inventory purchases, typically for up to </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><span><ix:nonNumeric id="d41150789e7224-wk-Fact-10E97C4C083F51508A8D6F417F1F8EB8" name="us-gaap:MaximumLengthOfTimeForeignCurrencyCashFlowHedge" contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD_us-gaap_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaap_ForeignExchangeContractMember" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">12</ix:nonNumeric> months</span></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">To protect the net investment in a foreign operation from fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, the Company may enter into foreign currency forward and option contracts to offset a portion of the changes in the carrying amounts of these investments due to fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates. In addition, the Company may use non-derivative financial instruments, such as its foreign currency&#8211;denominated debt, as hedges of its net investments in certain foreign subsidiaries. In both of these cases, the Company designates these instruments as net investment hedges.</span></div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">Apple Inc. | Q2 2019 Form 10-Q | </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">11</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><br/></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-577DF11D06B457DC9AF40D2FD05B9A19-4" continuedAt="TextSelection-577DF11D06B457DC9AF40D2FD05B9A19-5"><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-16E5C86F1D2C5813BC99BB86CBBE153D-2" continuedAt="TextSelection-16E5C86F1D2C5813BC99BB86CBBE153D-3"><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">To protect the Company&#8217;s foreign currency&#8211;denominated term debt or marketable securities from fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, the Company may enter into forward contracts, cross-currency swaps or other instruments. These instruments may offset a portion of the foreign currency remeasurement gains or losses, or changes in fair value. The Company may designate these instruments as either cash flow or fair value hedges. As of </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, the Company&#8217;s hedged term debt&#8211; and marketable securities&#8211;related foreign currency transactions are expected to be recognized within </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><span><ix:nonNumeric id="d41150789e7238-wk-Fact-2395A53BFF255182A444B97E012871AE" name="us-gaap:MaximumLengthOfTimeForeignCurrencyCashFlowHedge" contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD_us-gaap_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaap_CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember" format="ixt-sec:duryear">23</ix:nonNumeric> years</span></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company may also enter into non-designated foreign currency contracts to offset a portion of the foreign currency exchange gains and losses generated by the remeasurement of certain assets and liabilities denominated in non-functional currencies.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">To protect the Company&#8217;s foreign currency&#8211;denominated term debt or marketable securities from fluctuations in interest rates, the Company may enter into interest rate swaps, options or other instruments. These instruments may offset a portion of the changes in interest income or expense, or changes in fair value. The Company designates these instruments as either cash flow or fair value hedges. As of </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, the Company&#8217;s hedged interest rate transactions are expected to be recognized within </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><span><ix:nonNumeric id="d41150789e7252-wk-Fact-7E2C94BA92EC54189C8F49CCEBB3A3FA" name="us-gaap:MaximumLengthOfTimeHedgedInInterestRateCashFlowHedge1" contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD" format="ixt-sec:duryear">9</ix:nonNumeric> years</span></span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Cash Flow Hedges</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The effective portions of cash flow hedges are recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income/(loss) (&#8220;AOCI&#8221;) until the hedged item is recognized in earnings. Deferred gains and losses associated with cash flow hedges of foreign currency revenue are recognized as a component of net sales in the same period as the related revenue is recognized, and deferred gains and losses related to cash flow hedges of inventory purchases are recognized as a component of cost of sales in the same period as the related costs are recognized. Deferred gains and losses associated with cash flow hedges of interest income or expense are recognized in other income/(expense), net in the same period as the related income or expense is recognized. For options designated as cash flow hedges, changes in the time value are excluded from the assessment of hedge effectiveness. The ineffective portions and amounts excluded from the effectiveness testing of cash flow hedges are recognized in other income/(expense), net.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Derivative instruments designated as cash flow hedges must be de-designated as hedges when it is probable the forecasted hedged transaction will not occur in the initially identified time period or within a subsequent two-month time period. Deferred gains and losses in AOCI associated with such derivative instruments are reclassified into other income/(expense), net in the period of de-designation. Any subsequent changes in fair value of such derivative instruments are reflected in other income/(expense), net unless they are re-designated as hedges of other transactions.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Net Investment Hedges</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The effective portions of net investment hedges are recorded in OCI as a part of the cumulative translation adjustment. The ineffective portions and amounts excluded from the effectiveness testing of net investment hedges are recognized in other income/(expense), net. For foreign exchange forward contracts designated as net investment hedges, the Company excludes changes in fair value relating to changes in the forward carry component from its assessment of hedge effectiveness. Accordingly, any gains or losses related to this forward carry component are recognized in earnings in the current period.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Fair Value Hedges</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Gains and losses related to changes in fair value hedges are recognized in earnings along with a corresponding loss or gain related to the change in value of the underlying hedged item in the same line in the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations. For foreign exchange forward contracts designated as fair value hedges, the Company excludes changes in fair value relating to changes in the forward carry component from its assessment of hedge effectiveness. Although the table above reflects the notional and credit risk amounts of the Company&#8217;s derivative instruments, it does not reflect the gains or losses associated with the exposures and transactions that the instruments are intended to hedge. Therefore, many components used by the Company, including those that are available from multiple sources, are at times subject to industry-wide shortage and significant commodity pricing fluctuations that could materially adversely affect the Company&#8217;s financial condition and operating results.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company uses some custom components that are not commonly used by its competitors, and new products introduced by the Company often utilize custom components available from only one source. If the Company&#8217;s supply of components for a new or existing product were delayed or constrained, or if an outsourcing partner delayed shipments of completed products to the Company, the Company&#8217;s financial condition and operating results could be materially adversely affected. The Company&#8217;s business and financial performance could also be materially adversely affected depending on the time required to obtain sufficient quantities from the original source, or to identify and obtain sufficient quantities from an alternative source. Year-over-year services gross margin percentage increased during the </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">second</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> quarter and first six months of 2019 due primarily to a different services mix and leverage of the Company&#8217;s services fixed cost structure from higher services net sales, partially offset by the weakness in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company anticipates total gross margin percentage during the </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">third</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> quarter of </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> to be between 37.0% and 38.0%. The foregoing statement regarding the Company&#8217;s expected total gross margin percentage in the </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">third</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> quarter of </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> is forward-looking and could differ from actual results. The Company&#8217;s future gross margins can be impacted by multiple factors including, but not limited to, those set forth in Part II, Item 1A of this Form 10-Q under the heading &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; and those described in this paragraph. In general, the Company believes gross margins will be subject to volatility and remain under downward pressure due to a variety of factors, including: continued industry-wide global product pricing pressures and product pricing actions that the Company may take in response to such pressures; increased competition; the Company&#8217;s ability to effectively stimulate demand for certain of its products and services; compressed product life cycles; potential increases in the cost of components, outside manufacturing services, and acquiring and delivering content for the Company&#8217;s services; the Company&#8217;s ability to manage product quality and warranty costs effectively; shifts in the mix of products and services, or in the geographic, currency or channel mix; fluctuations in exchange rates; and costs associated with the Company&#8217;s frequent introductions and transitions of products and services.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div The Company&#8217;s effective tax rate for the first </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">six</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> months of </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> was lower compared to the same period in </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> due primarily to higher taxes in 2018 arising from the remeasurement of deferred tax assets and liabilities as a result of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the &#8220;Act&#8221;) and a lower statutory federal income tax rate in 2019, partially offset by higher taxes on foreign earnings in 2019.</span></div><div><a id="sE0EF40CAFBA750A198F9C4E846BC70B0"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:12px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Hedging</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In August 2017, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (the &#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) No. 2017-12, </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Derivatives and Hedging (Topic 815): Targeted Improvements to Accounting for Hedging Activities</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> (&#8220;ASU 2017-12&#8221;). ASU 2017-12 expands component and fair value hedging, specifies the presentation of the effects of hedging instruments, and eliminates the separate measurement and presentation of hedge ineffectiveness. The Company will adopt ASU 2017-12 in its first quarter of 2020 utilizing the modified retrospective transition method. Based on the Company&#8217;s derivative portfolio and hedging strategies, the adoption of ASU 2017-12 is not expected to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Financial Instruments</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In June 2016, the FASB issued ASU No. 2016-13, </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> (&#8220;ASU 2016-13&#8221;), which modifies the measurement of expected credit losses on certain financial instruments. The Company will adopt ASU 2016-13 in its first quarter of 2021 utilizing the modified retrospective transition method. Based on the composition of the Company&#8217;s investment portfolio, current market conditions, and historical credit loss activity, the adoption of ASU 2016-13 is not expected to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Leases</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU No. 2016-02, </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Leases (Topic 842)</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> (&#8220;ASU 2016-02&#8221;), which modifies lease accounting for lessees to increase transparency and comparability by recording lease assets and liabilities for operating leases and disclosing key information about leasing arrangements. The Company will adopt ASU 2016-02 utilizing the modified retrospective transition method through a cumulative-effect adjustment at the beginning of its first quarter of 2020. While the Company is currently evaluating the impact of adopting ASU 2016-02, based on the lease portfolio as of </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">March&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, the Company anticipates recording lease assets and liabilities of approximately $9 billion on its Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, with no material impact to its Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations. However, the ultimate impact of adopting ASU 2016-02 will depend on the Company&#8217;s lease portfolio as of the adoption date.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">Apple Inc. | Q2 2019 Form 10-Q | </span><span The iPhone Upgrade Program provides customers the right to trade in that iPhone for a specified amount when purchasing a new iPhone, provided certain conditions are met. The Company accounts for the trade-in right as a guarantee liability and recognizes arrangement revenue net of the fair value of such right, with subsequent changes to the guarantee liability recognized within net sales.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company has entered into indemnification agreements with its directors and executive officers. Under these agreements, the Company has agreed to indemnify such individuals to the fullest extent permitted by law against liabilities that arise by reason of their status as directors or officers of the Company, and to advance expenses incurred by such individuals in connection with related legal proceedings. It is not possible to determine the maximum potential amount of payments the Company could be required to make under these agreements due to the limited history of prior indemnification claims and the unique facts and circumstances involved in each claim. While the Company maintains directors and officers liability insurance coverage, such insurance coverage may be insufficient to cover all losses or all types of claims that may arise.</span></div><div><a id="sEAB2C2FAB38458019401693B11154B0A"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The preparation of financial statements and related disclosures in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and the Company&#8217;s discussion and analysis of its financial condition and operating results require the Company&#8217;s management to make judgments, assumptions and estimates that affect the amounts reported. Management bases its estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions it believes to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities. Actual results may differ from these estimates, and such differences may be material.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Note 1, &#8220;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#8221; in Part I, Item 1 of this Form 10-Q and in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, Item 8 of the </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> Form 10-K, and &#8220;Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates&#8221; in Part II, Item 7 of the </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"> Form 10-K describe the significant accounting policies and methods used in the preparation of the Company&#8217;s condensed consolidated financial statements. The first performance obligation, which represents the substantial portion of the allocated sales price, is the hardware and bundled software delivered at the time of sale. The second performance obligation is the right to receive certain product-related bundled services, which include iCloud, Siri and Maps. The third performance obligation is the right to receive, on a when-and-if-available basis, future unspecified software upgrades relating to the software bundled with each device. The Company allocates revenue and any related discounts to these performance obligations based on their relative stand-alone selling prices (&#8220;SSP&#8221;). Because the Company lacks observable prices for the undelivered performance obligations, the allocation of revenue is based on the Company&#8217;s estimated SSPs. Revenue allocated to the product-related bundled services and unspecified software upgrade rights is deferred and recognized on a straight-line basis over the estimated period they are expected to be provided. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company&#8217;s process for determining estimated SSPs involves management&#8217;s judgment and considers multiple factors that may vary over time depending upon the unique facts and circumstances related to each deliverable. Should future facts and circumstances change, the Company&#8217;s SSPs and the future rate of related amortization for unspecified software upgrades and services related to future sales of these devices could change. Factors subject to change include the nature of the unspecified software upgrade rights and product-related bundled services offered, their estimated value and the estimated period they are expected to be provided.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">Apple Inc. | Q2 2019 Form 10-Q | </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">33</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Impairment of Marketable Debt Securities</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company&#8217;s investments in marketable debt securities are classified as available-for-sale and reported at fair value. In making this determination, the Company evaluates, among other things, the duration and extent to which the fair value of a security is less than its cost; the financial condition of the issuer and any changes thereto; and the Company&#8217;s intent to sell, or whether it will more likely than not be required to sell, the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis. These and other economic factors could materially adversely affect the Company&#8217;s business, results of operations, financial condition and growth.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">Apple Inc. | Q2 2019 Form 10-Q | </span><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">35</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Global markets for the Company&#8217;s products and services are highly competitive and subject to rapid technological change, and the Company may be unable to compete effectively in these markets.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company&#8217;s products and services are offered in highly competitive global markets characterized by aggressive price competition and resulting downward pressure on gross margins, frequent introduction of new products and services, short product life cycles, evolving industry standards, continual improvement in product price/performance characteristics, rapid adoption of technological advancements by competitors and price sensitivity on the part of consumers and businesses.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company&#8217;s ability to compete successfully depends heavily on its ability to ensure a continuing and timely introduction of innovative new products, services and technologies to the marketplace. As a result, the Company must make significant investments in R&amp;D. There can be no assurance that these investments will achieve expected returns, and the Company may not be able to develop and market new products and services successfully.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Company currently holds a significant number of patents, trademarks and copyrights and has registered, and applied to register, numerous patents, trademarks and copyrights.     <us-gaap:BasisOfPresentationAndSignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-7DB85DDB7DC357B6B30014CEF2E6F351-0-wk-Fact-DFF4BBADE87A52E89D7B6DDDD4F60705">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:12px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Basis of Presentation and Preparation&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The accompanying condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Apple Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries (collectively &#x201c;Apple&#x201d; or the &#x201c;Company&#x201d;). Intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated. In the opinion of the Company&#x2019;s management, the condensed consolidated financial statements reflect all adjustments, which are normal and recurring in nature, necessary for fair financial statement presentation. The preparation of these condensed consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported. Actual results could differ materially from those estimates. Certain prior period amounts in the condensed consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes have been reclassified to conform to the current period&#x2019;s presentation. These condensed consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes should be read in conjunction with the Company&#x2019;s annual consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto included in its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;29, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; (the &#x201c;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; Form 10-K&#x201d;).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company&#x2019;s fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September. A 14th week is included in the first fiscal quarter every five or six years to realign the Company&#x2019;s fiscal quarters with calendar quarters. The Company&#x2019;s fiscal years 2019 and 2018 span 52 weeks each. Unless otherwise stated, references to particular years, quarters, months and periods refer to the Company&#x2019;s fiscal years ended in September and the associated quarters, months and periods of those fiscal years.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:12px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Revenue Recognition&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;In the first quarter of 2019, the Company adopted the Financial Accounting Standards Board&#x2019;s (the &#x201c;FASB&#x201d;) Accounting Standards Update (&#x201c;ASU&#x201d;) No. 2014-09, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; (&#x201c;ASU 2014-09&#x201d;), and additional ASUs issued to clarify the guidance in ASU 2014-09 (collectively the &#x201c;new revenue standard&#x201d;), which amends the existing accounting standards for revenue recognition.&#160;The Company adopted the new revenue standard utilizing the full retrospective transition method. The Company did not restate total net sales in the prior periods presented, as adoption of the new revenue standard did not have a material impact on previously reported amounts.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Additionally, beginning in the first quarter of 2019, the Company classified the amortization of the deferred value of Maps, Siri&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and free iCloud&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; services, which are bundled in the sales price of iPhone&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, Mac&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, iPad&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and certain other products, in services net sales. Historically, the Company classified the amortization of these amounts in products net sales consistent with its management reporting framework. As a result, products and services net sales information for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;second&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; quarter and first &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; months of 2018 was reclassified to conform to the 2019 presentation.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Financial Instruments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;In the first quarter of 2019, the Company adopted FASB ASU No. 2016-01, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Financial Instruments &#x2013; Overall (Subtopic 825-10): Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; (&#x201c;ASU 2016-01&#x201d;), which updates certain aspects of the recognition, measurement, presentation and disclosure of financial instruments. The adoption of ASU 2016-01 did not have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s condensed consolidated financial statements.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Income Taxes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;In the first quarter of 2019, the Company adopted FASB ASU No. 2016-16, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Income Taxes (Topic 740): Intra-Entity Transfers of Assets Other Than Inventory&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; (&#x201c;ASU 2016-16&#x201d;), which requires the recognition of the income tax consequences of an intra-entity transfer of an asset, other than inventory, when the transfer occurs. The Company adopted ASU 2016-16 utilizing the modified retrospective transition method. Upon adoption, the Company recorded &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.7 billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of net deferred tax assets, reduced other non-current assets by &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$128 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and increased retained earnings by &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.6 billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; on its Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet. The Company will recognize incremental deferred income tax expense as these net deferred tax assets are utilized.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Restricted quarter of 2019, the Company adopted FASB ASU No. 2016-18, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Statement of Cash Flows (Topic 230): Restricted Cash&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; (&#x201c;ASU 2016-18&#x201d;), which enhances and clarifies the guidance on the classification and The Company did not restate total net sales in the prior periods presented, as adoption of the new revenue standard did not have a material impact on previously reported amounts.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Additionally, beginning in the first quarter of 2019, the Company classified the amortization of the deferred value of Maps, Siri&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and free iCloud&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; services, which are bundled in the sales price of iPhone&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, Mac&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, iPad&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and certain other products, in services net sales.     <aapl:RestrictedCashandMarketableSecuritiesPolicyTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-D4A8A96EB845FE4A1007A14277E232B4-0-wk-Fact-67A9F494A2408B2DDE0FA158695984C4">The Company considers cash and marketable securities to be restricted when withdrawal or general use is legally restricted. The Company records restricted cash as other assets in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, and determines current or non-current classification based on the expected duration of the restriction. The Company records restricted marketable securities as current or non-current marketable securities in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets based on the classification of the underlying securities.</aapl:RestrictedCashandMarketableSecuritiesPolicyTextBlock>
    <us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-56E78E41ABE2572892B7E0E0DC6845BB-0-wk-Fact-0B0FF259ED3B5B7A83DB2AE393343468">Revenue Recognition&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Net sales consist of revenue from the sale of iPhone, Mac, iPad, services and other products. The Company recognizes revenue at the amount to which it expects to be entitled when control of the products or services is transferred to its customers. Control is generally transferred when the Company has a present right to payment and title and the significant risks and rewards of ownership of products or services are transferred to its customers. For most of the Company&#x2019;s products net sales, control transfers when products are shipped. For the Company&#x2019;s services net sales, control transfers over time as services are delivered. Payment for products and services net sales is collected within a short period of time following transfer of control or commencement of delivery of services, as applicable.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company records reductions to products net sales related to future product returns, price protection and other customer incentive programs based on the Company&#x2019;s expectations and historical experience.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;For arrangements with multiple performance obligations, which represent promises within an arrangement that are capable of being distinct, the Company allocates revenue to all distinct performance obligations based on their relative stand-alone selling prices (&#x201c;SSP&#x201d;). When available, the Company uses observable prices to determine the SSP. When observable prices are not available, SSPs are established that reflect the Company&#x2019;s best estimates of what the selling prices of the performance obligations would be if they were sold regularly on a stand-alone basis. The Company&#x2019;s process for estimating SSPs without observable prices considers multiple factors that may vary depending upon the unique facts and circumstances related to each performance obligation including, where applicable, prices charged by the Company for similar offerings, market trends in the pricing for similar offerings, product-specific business objectives and the estimated cost to provide the performance obligation.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company has identified up to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; performance obligations regularly included in arrangements involving the sale of iPhone, Mac, iPad and certain other products. The first performance obligation, which represents the substantial portion of the allocated sales price, is the hardware and bundled software delivered at the time of sale. The second performance obligation is the right to receive certain product-related bundled services, which include iCloud, Siri and Maps. The third performance obligation is the right to receive, on a when-and-if-available basis, future unspecified software upgrades relating to the software bundled with each device. The Company allocates revenue and any related discounts to these performance obligations based on their relative SSPs. Because the Company lacks observable prices for the undelivered performance obligations, the allocation of revenue is based on the Company&#x2019;s estimated SSPs. Revenue allocated to the delivered hardware and bundled software is recognized when control has transferred to the customer, which generally occurs when the product is shipped. Revenue allocated to the product-related bundled services and unspecified software upgrade rights is deferred and recognized on a straight-line basis over the estimated period they are expected to be provided. Cost of sales related to delivered hardware and bundled software, including estimated warranty costs, are recognized at the time of sale. Costs incurred to provide product-related bundled services and unspecified software upgrade rights are recognized as cost of sales as incurred.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;For certain long-term service arrangements, the Company has performance obligations for services it has not yet delivered. For these arrangements, the Company does not have a right to bill for the undelivered services. The Company has determined that any unbilled consideration relates entirely to the value of the undelivered services. Accordingly, the Company has not recognized revenue, and has elected not to disclose amounts, related to these undelivered services.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;For the sale of third-party products where the Company obtains control of the product before transferring it to the customer, the Company recognizes revenue based on the gross amount billed to customers. The Company considers multiple factors when determining whether it obtains control of third-party products including, but not limited to, evaluating if it has the ability to establish the price of the product, retains inventory risk for tangible products or has the responsibility for ensuring acceptability of the product. For third-party applications sold through the App Store&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, Mac App Store and TV App Store and certain digital content sold through the iTunes Store&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company does not obtain control of the product before transferring it to the customer. Therefore, the Company accounts for such sales on a net basis by recognizing in services net sales only the commission it retains.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company has elected to record revenue net of taxes collected from customers that are remitted to governmental authorities, with the collected taxes recorded within other current liabilities until remitted to the relevant government authority.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:24px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Deferred Revenue&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:8px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;30, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;29, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company had total deferred revenue of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$8.2 billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$8.8 billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;March&#160;30, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;1%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in greater     <us-gaap:RevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-326B9DD94A8C5048A7C675DBC3ECD37E-0-wk-Fact-E60E0CA545AB59A39C0C2730F1A66B41">Net sales consist of revenue from the sale of iPhone, Mac, iPad, services and other products. The Company recognizes revenue at the amount to which it expects to be entitled when control of the products or services is transferred to its customers. Control is generally transferred when the Company has a present right to payment and title and the significant risks and rewards of ownership of products or services are transferred to its customers. For most of the Company&#x2019;s products net sales, control transfers when products are shipped. For the Company&#x2019;s services net sales, control transfers over time as services are delivered. Payment for products and services net sales is collected within a short period of time following transfer of control or commencement of delivery of services, as applicable.&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company records reductions to products net sales related to future product returns, price protection and other customer incentive programs based on the Company&#x2019;s expectations and historical experience.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;For arrangements with multiple performance obligations, which represent promises within an arrangement that are capable of being distinct, the Company allocates revenue to all distinct performance obligations based on their relative stand-alone selling prices (&#x201c;SSP&#x201d;). When available, the Company uses observable prices to determine the SSP. When observable prices are not available, SSPs are established that reflect the Company&#x2019;s best estimates of what the selling prices of the performance obligations would be if they were sold regularly on a stand-alone basis. The Company&#x2019;s process for estimating SSPs without observable prices considers multiple factors that may vary depending upon the unique facts and circumstances related to each performance obligation including, where applicable, prices charged by the Company for similar offerings, market trends in the pricing for similar offerings, product-specific business objectives and the estimated cost to provide the performance obligation.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company has identified up to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt; performance obligations regularly included in arrangements involving the sale of iPhone, Mac, iPad and certain other products. The first performance obligation, which represents the substantial portion of the allocated sales price, is the hardware and bundled software delivered at the time of sale. The second performance obligation is the right to receive certain product-related bundled services, which include iCloud, Siri and Maps. The third performance obligation is the right to receive, on a when-and-if-available basis, future unspecified software upgrades relating to the software bundled with each device. The Company allocates revenue and any related discounts to these performance obligations based on their relative SSPs. Because the Company lacks observable prices for the undelivered performance obligations, the allocation of revenue is based on the Company&#x2019;s estimated SSPs. Revenue allocated to the delivered hardware and bundled software is recognized when control has transferred to the customer, which generally occurs when the product is shipped. Revenue allocated to the product-related bundled services and unspecified software upgrade rights is deferred and recognized on a straight-line basis over the estimated period they are expected to be provided. Cost of sales related to delivered hardware and bundled software, including estimated warranty costs, are recognized at the time of sale. Costs incurred to provide product-related bundled services and unspecified software upgrade rights are recognized as cost of sales as incurred.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;For certain long-term service arrangements, the Company has performance obligations for services it has not yet delivered. For these arrangements, the Company does not have a right to bill for the undelivered services. The Company has determined that any unbilled consideration relates entirely to the value of the undelivered services. Accordingly, the Company has not recognized revenue, and has elected not to disclose amounts, related to these undelivered services.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;For the sale of third-party products where the Company obtains control of the product before transferring it to the customer, the Company recognizes revenue based on the gross amount billed to customers. The Company considers multiple factors when determining whether it obtains control of third-party products including, but not limited to, evaluating if it has the ability to establish the price of the product, retains inventory risk for tangible products or has the responsibility for ensuring acceptability of the product. For third-party applications sold through the App Store&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, Mac App Store and TV App Store and certain digital content sold through the iTunes Store&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company does not obtain control of the product before transferring it to the customer. Therefore, the Company accounts for such sales on a net basis by recognizing in services net sales only the commission it retains.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;The Company has elected to record revenue net of taxes collected from customers that are remitted to governmental authorities, with the collected taxes recorded within other current liabilities until remitted to the relevant government authority.</us-gaap:RevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock>
